title: QBR - NovaEdge Health Check
summary: Quarterly business review focused on usage growth, cost drift on embeddings, two reliability incidents in Feb, alignment on roadmap items (KV cache tuning, dedicated burst capacity), and next steps to run benchmarks for Private pilot and share security docs.
next_steps: Redwood to send detailed cost/usage breakdown and embedding recommendations (Alex) - by 2026-03-24
Schedule technical deep-dive to scope Private deployment pilot (Marco + Lee) - week of 2026-03-30
Share SOC2/ISO docs and network architecture notes (Priya) - by 2026-03-20
Provide sample SLA language for Dedicated plan (Daniel) - by 2026-03-25
action_items: Alex: send cost breakdown and suggested quantization/profile changes (due 2026-03-24)
Marco: schedule 90-min technical deep dive to run perf benchmarks (due 2026-03-30)
Priya: share SOC2 and audit log spec, and link to security pack (due 2026-03-20)
Lee (NovaEdge): provide recent p95/p99 latency logs and top prompt examples (due 2026-03-22)
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Morgan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we wanted to do a quick qbr slash health check for the last quarter so we can, you know, align on usage trends and any blocker for the private pilot.
[00:12] Jordan Lee: yep thanks alex, we've got most of the team on. jordan here, sam and lee will chime in for the infra bits, aisha for security.
[00:22] Priya Patel: quick note on agenda, we'll cover usage & costs, reliability incidents, open roadmap items you asked about, and then next steps for the pilot.
[00:32] Sam Patel: sounds good. i saw the usage dashboard—embedding calls spiked in feb with the new semantic search batch. curious what you recommend for cost ops.
[00:42] Alex Morgan: yeah so embeddings are the big driver. we pulled a detailed breakdown. overall tokens/generation maintain steady, embeddings are 62% of spend last 30 days. i can share a spreadsheet after this.
[00:56] Lee Nguyen: cost's one thing, but latency for search also matters—p95 for embeddings lookup is creeping up during peak. we had 2 incidents in feb where p99 jumped.
[01:10] Marco Rivera: right, and on the infra side the incidents were related to cache warm-up and burst capacity. a couple notes: we recommended KV cache tuning and a small increase in reserved capacity for the nightly reindex job.
[01:25] Jordan Lee: can you remind us which cache mode you recommend? we were on the default prefix cache, i think.
[01:31] Marco Rivera: yes default prefix. for your workload pattern (large batch reindex followed by many small lookups) we suggest enabling continuous prefix cache and setting a higher shared cache size — that will cut the hot-path latency. also some quantization for the embedder can reduce cost on dedicated.
[01:45] Sam Patel: quantization sounds interesting—what's the tradeoff on quality? we can't lose recall for our semantic matching.
[01:52] Alex Morgan: good question. in our bench tests for similar models we saw sub-1% recall delta for 4-bit quant on embeddings if you calibrate on your sample prompts. we'll include recommended calibration prompts in the cost report.
[02:06] Aisha Khan: on security, we need SOC2 + audit logs and details on KMS integration for the private pilot. also SSO, RBAC mapping — we have to show this to compliance.
[02:18] Priya Patel: absolutely, we'll share the security pack and a network diagram. priya typing the link in chat now (link: redwood.com/security-pack) — i'll also include KMS/HSM integration notes.
[02:32] Jordan Lee: thanks. timeline-wise, we're hoping to run a pilot for private deployment in q2 if the pilot results look good. do you see any blockers for that schedule?
[02:41] Daniel Cho: from product side we can support a minimal private control plane setup for you. main items to finalize: capacity sizing, E2E perf benchmarks, and SOC docs. Marco can lead the technical scope.
[02:52] Marco Rivera: i'll propose a 90-minute session with lee and sam to reproduce your perf pattern and run a DB of prompt sets. we can instrument KV hit rate, batching efficiency, and end-to-end p95/p99.
[03:05] Lee Nguyen: that works. we can share a sample of the nightly index job, and the search traffic profile.
[03:12] Sam Patel: another thing—model drift checks. we've seen small regressions with a new model family you rolled out last month; can we get per-model quality deltas?
[03:22] Alex Morgan: yes, we have eval hooks and we can run a quick regression test across your golden prompts. we'll attach the evaluation results to the cost report.
[03:31] Jordan Lee: about pricing — our finance wants to understand committed vs burst pricing. we don't want unexpected bills if we have a spike.
[03:40] Alex Morgan: for Dedicated we can do reserved capacity with burst buckets and caps. i'll include a sample commitment schedule. for hosted usage we can set alerts and quota caps.
[03:52] Aisha Khan: and retention — how long are logs and transcripts kept in hosted? we need retention policies that match our legal.
[03:59] Priya Patel: default retention is 90 days for transcripts and logs in hosted, but for Dedicated/Private you control retention; we also have longer retention add-ons. we'll send the retention options doc.
[04:12] Jordan Lee: good. can you summarize the feb reliability incidents? giving detail helps our SRE post-mortem.
[04:20] Marco Rivera: quick summary: Feb 3rd incident — high latency during a large batch reindex, root cause: cache thrash caused by simultaneous large KV writes and read-heavy queries. Feb 18th incident — transient GPU node reboot during scheduled maintenance which triggered a small spike until fallback routing engaged. both incidents had fallbacks but impacted p99 for ~8-18 minutes.
[04:47] Lee Nguyen: were there any data-loss or correctness issues?
[04:50] Marco Rivera: no data loss. correctness unaffected. we had degraded latency only. we've suggested autoscaling policy tweaks and improved fallback thresholds.
[04:58] Sam Patel: ok that's acceptable as long as we get tighter p99 guarantees.
[05:02] Daniel Cho: we can propose SLA language for p95/p99 on Dedicated; i'll draft a sample and send it.
[05:09] Jordan Lee: for the private pilot, will you provide a pre-packaged on-prem image or a helm chart?
[05:15] Marco Rivera: both options exist—VPC control plane for cloud private and a helm chart for on-prem. for quick proof we'll usually start with a VPC/private AWS deployment.
[05:25] Lee Nguyen: network-wise we'll need explicit IP allowlists and transit gateway notes.
[05:30] Priya Patel: we'll include network appendix and sample IaC.
[05:35] Sam Patel: can we run initial benchmarks on a small node set and then scale up? we don't want to provision a huge fleet up front.
[05:41] Alex Morgan: yes, we'll run scaling tests and show economic curves — cost per 1k requests at small, medium, large cluster sizes.
[05:48] Aisha Khan: please also include KMS key rotation policies and support for customer-managed keys. that's a must.
[05:55] Priya Patel: yes, note added.
[06:00] Jordan Lee: circling back — next steps and owners?
[06:05] Alex Morgan: i'll push cost/usage breakdown and recommended quantization/profile changes by next tuesday 2026-03-24.
[06:12] Marco Rivera: i'll send invite for the 90-min technical deep-dive and attach initial bench plan, target week of 2026-03-30.
[06:19] Priya Patel: i'll share SOC2/ISO and audit pack by 2026-03-20.
[06:25] Lee Nguyen: i'll gather the p95/p99 logs and sample prompts and send them before the deep dive (by 2026-03-22).
[06:32] Jordan Lee: perfect. if we get positive pilot numbers we can talk committed Dedicated capacity mid-april.
[06:39] Alex Morgan: excellent. any other questions?
[06:43] Sam Patel: quick one — are there any immediate quick wins to reduce cost before the pilot? small config changes?
[06:49] Marco Rivera: yes — short term: increase prefix cache size, enable continuous caching, and apply embedder quantization on lower-importance indexes. we'll list per-index recommendations in the report.
[07:05] Jordan Lee: thanks everyone, will wait for the notes.
[07:09] Priya Patel: thanks all — will record action items and follow up via the crm.
[07:15] Alex Morgan: thanks folks, end of meeting.

Notes/References: shared link to cost dashboard and security pack in chat. transcription imperfect in spots (noise and overlapping talk).
notes: Spreadsheet: cost breakdown (to be shared by Alex)
